nodes.title: Role-based access control: Key Ideas
nodes.content: RBAC assigns permissions to roles, then users to roles — a layer of indirection that scales. Azure's RBAC, AWS's IAM, Kubernetes RBAC, and GCP's IAM all share the same mental model. Mastering one transfers directly to the others.

flashcards.front: Why use roles instead of granting permissions to users directly?
flashcards.back: Roles separate WHO from WHAT. Add a person to a role, they inherit the permissions. Remove them, they lose access instantly. Auditing: 'who can read prod?' becomes 'who's in the prod-readers role?' instead of scanning thousands of user-level policies. Onboarding/offboarding becomes role membership changes, not 500 permission grants.

flashcards.front: What's the difference between a built-in role and a custom role?
flashcards.back: Built-in: cloud-provided, covers common patterns (Owner, Contributor, Reader, Storage Admin). Can't be modified. Custom: you define the exact actions allowed — pick when built-ins are too broad or too narrow. Cost of custom roles: maintenance — every new service adds actions you may need to add.

flashcards.front: Scope — why is it as important as the role?
flashcards.back: Same role at different scopes = wildly different power. 'Contributor' at the subscription scope = god mode on the whole subscription. 'Contributor' on one resource group = limited to that group's resources. Always scope at the smallest unit that's practical — never grant subscription-level if resource-group-level works.

flashcards.front: RBAC vs ABAC — when do you need attributes?
flashcards.back: RBAC: permissions tied to fixed roles. Works great until you need rules like 'engineers can read their own team's resources but not others'. ABAC (attribute-based) evaluates request attributes (user.team, resource.team) at runtime. Most clouds support both — start with RBAC, add ABAC tags when the role explosion becomes painful.

pairs.stem: A worker node needs to join an existing cluster but the bootstrap token has expired. Which kubeadm command generates a new join token?
You are initializing a new Kubernetes control plane with kubeadm. You want the API server to advertise the IP address 10.0.1.100 to worker nodes. Which kubeadm init flag should you use?

You have multiple clusters defined in your kubeconfig. You need to temporarily switch to a cluster named 'prod-cluster' for the next few commands. Which command sets the active context without permanently modifying the config?
You need to prevent new pods from being scheduled on a node 'worker-3' while allowing existing pods to continue running, so you can perform maintenance. Which command achieves this?
When bootstrapping a cluster with kubeadm, which flag allows you to specify a custom pod network CIDR for the CNI plugin?
A developer reports that 'kubectl get pods' returns 'Error from server (Forbidden)'. Their kubeconfig context is correct and points to the cluster. What is the most likely root cause?
pairs.option: The developer's user or ServiceAccount lacks a Role or ClusterRole binding granting 'get' on pods

nodes.title: Troubleshooting methodology: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A structured troubleshooting process beats random guessing every time. The classic flow: identify the problem precisely, form a theory, test it, fix, verify, document. Most exams test that you know the flow AND can spot the layer at which the symptom originates.

flashcards.back: CompTIA's 6-step: (1) Identify the problem (gather symptoms, questions to user, recent changes). (2) Establish a theory of probable cause. (3) Test the theory. (4) Plan and implement the fix. (5) Verify full system functionality, apply preventive measures. (6) Document everything.

flashcards.front: Top-down vs bottom-up troubleshooting on a network problem.
flashcards.back: Top-down: start at the application layer and work down — does the browser work? DNS? TCP? Routing? Bottom-up: start at the physical layer — is the cable plugged in? Link light? IP? When you suspect physical/cable, bottom-up is faster. When the user has 'a website is broken', top-down is faster.

Almost every production incident traces back to a recent change — a deploy, a config push, a vendor patch, a cert rotation. 'It was working yesterday' tells you to check today's change-log before forming an exotic theory. Recent changes are the highest-priors of the bug space.

Bisect the path between symptom and cause. If 10 hops between client and server, test hop 5. Good → problem is past hop 5. Bad → problem is before. Two more bisections narrow it to one hop. Faster than checking every link sequentially when the chain is long.

pairs.stem: You need a DaemonSet to run on every node including control plane nodes, which have the taint 'node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule'. What must you add to the DaemonSet pod spec?
pairs.option: Add a toleration for 'node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane' with effect 'NoSchedule'

pairs.stem: A StatefulSet 'db' has 3 replicas. You notice that 'db-2' is stuck in Pending while 'db-0' and 'db-1' are Running. What is the default StatefulSet behavior that causes this sequencing?
pairs.option: The StatefulSet waits for a rolling update to complete before creating new pods

pairs.stem: You want a pod to prefer scheduling on nodes labeled 'disktype=ssd' but still schedule on other nodes if no SSD nodes are available. Which scheduling construct should you use?
pairs.option: A required NodeAffinity with matchExpressions on disktype=ssd

pairs.stem: You need to expose a Service externally using a cloud provider's load balancer. Which Service type should you use?

A pod is stuck in 'Pending' state. 'kubectl describe pod my-pod' shows: 'Warning FailedScheduling: 0/4 nodes are available: 4 Insufficient memory.' The pod requests 8Gi memory. What is the most appropriate fix?
pairs.option: Either add a node with sufficient memory to the cluster.

pairs.stem: A Job must run exactly 6 pod completions with no more than 2 pods running at the same time. Which Job spec fields should you configure?

pairs.stem: A pod is in 'OOMKilled' status. 'kubectl describe pod crashed-pod' shows 'Last State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled'. What does this indicate and what is the correct remediation?
pairs.option: The container exceeded its memory limit;.

pairs.stem: A node shows status 'NotReady'. You SSH into the node and run 'systemctl status kubelet'. It shows 'Active: failed'. What is your next diagnostic step?
pairs.option: Delete and recreate the node object in Kubernetes

pairs.stem: A PersistentVolumeClaim is stuck in 'Pending' state. 'kubectl describe pvc my-pvc' shows: 'no persistent volumes available for this claim and no storage class is set'. What is missing?
pairs.option: The PVC needs a nodeAffinity selector to find a node with local storage

pairs.stem: You need a volume that is shared between two containers in the same pod and is deleted when the pod is removed. Which volume type should you use?
You need to mount a secret as a volume in a pod so the application can read the secret values as files. Which volume type and mount configuration achieves this?
pairs.option: Use a 'secret' volume type referencing the Secret name.

pairs.stem: The kube-scheduler pod is not running after a cluster upgrade. It is defined as a static pod. Where would you find its manifest to investigate?

pairs.stem: A pod's application writes logs to /var/log/app.log inside the container. 'kubectl logs' shows nothing. What is the most likely reason?
pairs.option: kubectl logs only captures stdout and stderr.

pairs.stem: You need to check why the kube-controller-manager is continuously restarting. Which command retrieves its previous container's logs?
You need to check the container runtime version and status on a node where Docker is not installed (containerd is used). Which command should you use on the node?
A node is running many pods and you want to identify which pod is consuming the most memory at this moment. Which kubectl command gives you per-pod memory usage on a specific node?

A node's disk pressure condition is True. You run 'kubectl describe node worker-1' and see 'DiskPressure: True'. As a result, some pods are being evicted. What is the underlying cause and immediate remediation?
pairs.option: The node's filesystem (typically /var/lib/kubelet or /var/lib/docker or container image storage) is near capacity; free up disk space by removing unused images, logs, or data

pairs.stem: A Deployment has a readinessProbe that fails during startup. As a result, Service traffic is never routed to the new pods. The pods are Running but not Ready. Which Deployment field can you configure so that startup failures don't count as readiness failures during a defined grace period?
